name: Forma / Forma-i
lead: Forma and Forma-i are radiofrequency (RF) devices from the aesthetics company InMode that are used in clinics for non-surgical skin tightening of the face and body. Practitioners offer them to firm lax skin along the jawline, cheeks and neck, giving a tighter, more defined lower face without surgery. Treatment is delivered in a series of sessions, and a 2022 study of the Forma device on the chin and neck area used four sessions over about six weeks [2].

Radiofrequency skin tightening works by heating the deeper layers of skin to stimulate the body to make new collagen, elastin and hyaluronic acid, which is intended to soften fine lines and lift loose skin; Wikipedia presents it as a non-surgical alternative to facelifts [1]. People in looksmaxxing circles file facial RF under non-invasive "hardmaxxing" procedures, alongside other clinic-based treatments aimed at jawline and skin definition.

A published study of Forma in 22 patients with submental laxity found significant improvements in laxity scores and fat volume, with transient redness and no serious side effects [2]. This entry describes the treatment in general terms; protocols are set by clinics and the manufacturer.

chain: Heating prompts collagen and elastin remodelling
Skin looks firmer and the jawline and cheeks look tighter
angle.text: Clinics use facial RF to tighten loose skin around the jowls, cheeks and neck, which can give a sharper lower-face outline. Treatment is non-surgical and is usually done as a series of sessions.

infobox: Four sessions over about six weeks (submental area)

paras: RF devices pass radio-frequency energy through the skin to heat the dermis. The heat is intended to trigger collagen, elastin and hyaluronic acid production, and a dermal temperature of about 67 degrees Celsius has been described as ideal for remodelling and reducing wrinkles and laxity [1]. Penetration depth depends on the electrode design, with monopolar, bipolar and unipolar arrangements in use [1]. The submental study described the device as bipolar radiofrequency [2].
Wikipedia adds that manipulating skin cooling during treatment lets RF also heat deeper tissue and reduce fat [1].

RF skin tightening is used on the jowls, abdomen, thighs and arms, and for wrinkle reduction, cellulite and body contouring [1]. In facial work the usual aim is a firmer, tighter-looking lower face and neck. Related RF devices include Thermage, Venus Legacy, Exilis and microneedle RF systems [1].

Reported effects of RF treatments in general include pain significant enough to require sedation in some patients, surface dents from uneven healing when energy is applied improperly, and, rarely, fat necrosis and atrophic scarring; applying vacuum at the site reportedly reduced burning and crusting [1]. In the Forma submental study almost all subjects had transient redness right after treatment and no serious side effects were reported [2].

A 2022 study in the Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology by Chawvavanich, Singthong and Intarachaieua treated 22 patients with submental laxity on both sides of the submental area using Forma in four sessions over about six weeks. Two blinded dermatologists scored photographs before and after treatment, and the study reported significant improvement on the physical assessment scale after the third session, significant improvement in the laxity score after the second session, and significant fat-volume reduction from one week to six months after baseline [2]. It appears to be an uncontrolled treatment series [2].
Broader studies of radiofrequency skin tightening, including a blinded randomised comparison of fractional RF and surgical facelift for skin laxity, are listed in Wikipedia without results [1].

timeline.event: Study of Forma bipolar radiofrequency for submental laxity published in the Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology [2].

card.summary: InMode radiofrequency treatment that heats the skin to tighten the jawline, cheeks and neck without surgery.
card.note: Pain, uneven healing and rare scarring have been reported with RF treatments in general.

quick.overview:
Forma and Forma-i are InMode radiofrequency devices used in clinics to tighten skin on the face and body. The idea is to warm the deeper skin so it builds fresh collagen, giving a firmer, lifted look along the jawline and cheeks.

It is non-surgical and typically delivered over several sessions by a clinician.
quick.mechanism: RF energy heats the dermis, which is intended to stimulate collagen, elastin and hyaluronic acid production and so reduce laxity and fine lines.
quick.risks: RF treatments in general have been associated with pain, dents from uneven healing, and rarely fat necrosis or scarring; newer techniques aim to reduce these.
